case_title: Arumugam v. State represented by its Inspector of Police
accused_occupation: Agriculturist (as described for the family members named in the judgment, including the appellant's family)
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (step-son and step-mother); prior friction over the victim's conduct, which the accused disapproved of and had often asked her to change
evidence_type: Extra-judicial confession (oral to a witness and written statement to the Village Administrative Officer); medical evidence; recovery of rope; witness testimony of step-sister
confession: Extra-judicial confession made to the step-sister and then to the Village Administrative Officer (written as Ex.P1); relied on by the Court
aggravating_circumstances: Planning (rope hidden in field earlier); annoyance over victim's conduct as motive
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302; sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal against conviction dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
neutral_facts: A woman, the second wife of the accused's father, was killed in a field adjoining a village. The accused had been unhappy with the victim's conduct and had repeatedly asked her to behave in a dignified way, but she had replied that her life was her own affair. On the day of the incident, the victim and her step-daughter went to the field to do agricultural work. Later, the accused called the victim to help lift a bundle of firewood, and both walked into a sugarcane field. Shortly afterwards the accused returned alone and told the step-daughter that the victim had been strangled and killed. Around 4 p.m. the accused also told the Village Administrative Officer that the accused had murdered the victim. The officer recorded this in writing and took the accused to the police station, where a case was registered. The investigating officer recovered a rope on the accused's statement. The post-mortem, performed the next day, found a ligature mark about 3 cm wide encircling the neck. The doctor found death by asphyxia due to strangulation, occurring 27 to 30 hours before the autopsy. The step-daughter's husband and the accused's father did not support the prosecution. A charge sheet was filed after the investigation.
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia due to strangulation; 3 cm ligature mark around neck; no other injuries showing a struggle
premeditation_planning: Yes: Court found the accused prepared for the day and hid the rope in the field earlier
motive: Annoyance at the victim's conduct, the accused suspecting her of low character and finding her an embarrassment
key_evidence_accepted: Extra-judicial confession to step-sister and Village Administrative Officer; PW5's admission about accused's annoyance; medical evidence of strangulation and time of death; rope recovery
witness_credibility: Step-sister's evidence accepted, including her admission about the accused's annoyance; hostile father and brother-in-law's evidence held not to undermine the case; medical evidence held to support the ocular account
post_offence_conduct: Disclosed the killing to step-sister and then to the Village Administrative Officer; did not try to run away; handed over to police
trial_duration: offence: 19 March 2000; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 01.09.2005; Supreme Court: July 28, 2010
legal_representation: Accused: Venkat Subramanyam, V. K. Sidharthan, Anup Kumar; State: S. Thananjayan
investigation_status: FIR registered on extra-judicial confession; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: None noted (defence argued the 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. gap in FIR registration was unexplained; the Court did not treat it as a lapse)
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, life imprisonment under s.302; High Court: appeal dismissed; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Conviction rests on sound appreciation of evidence; extra-judicial confession to PW1 should not be discarded; medical evidence supports the prosecution story
defence_argument: Conviction solely on extra-judicial confession unjustified as father, step-sister and brother-in-law turned hostile; 4 p.m./6 p.m. FIR delay unexplained; medical evidence contradicted by decomposed body; victim too strong to be strangled
legal_principle_applied: Extra-judicial confession is weak evidence but may be relied on where distinctive features (prompt disclosure, no flight, corroboration) exist; hostile witnesses did not undermine the case; medical evidence must be consistent with ocular evidence
judicial_aggravating_factors: Premeditation and planning, including concealing the rope in advance
